newsitem.title: USA: White House sees continued strong ties with France.
newsitem.headline: White House sees continued strong ties with France.

text.p: The United States expects continuation of "active, productive, warm" Franco-American relations following the election of a Socialist government in France, President Bill Clinton's spokesman said on Monday.

"We've got enduring interests that we explore through our close and bilateral relationship with France, and at a time when the future of Europe is very much on the minds of those of us in the United States...we would seek a very active, productive, warm relationship with all elements of the French government," spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
In response to a question about possible change in French policy toward Bosnia, McCurry said U.S. officials anticipated "continuity more than change" in France's foreign policy.

The election left Clinton and French President Jacques Chirac in a similiar position, having to work in tandem with their political opposition. Earlier in the day, McCurry was diplomatic when asked if Clinton, who has faced Republican control of Congress since 1994, had any advice for Chirac.
"Well, the French political culture is much different than the political climate in the United States, but we ourselves have something of cohabitation. We know it can work," Clinton's spokesman said.
When asked about how the election would affect the push for a common currency in Europe as part of European Economic and Monetary Union, or EMU, McCurry replied with a wisecrack.
"The EMU, for the benefit of those of you who don't know, is not a small furry creature that's on the endangered list," he quipped, referring to the flightless bird called an emu.

McCurry went on to note Treasury Secretrary Robert Rubin had recently said an integrated currency in Europe was good for global currency markets, and added that Rubin was "the authoritative spokesman on the issue."
In Paris, French officials said Clinton telephoned Chirac on Monday evening and the two men had a "warm and friendly conversation".
They recalled that the two are scheduled to meet in Denver on June 20 at an annual summit of leaders of the world's leading industrialised countries.
